<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **2** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b4c99b8dd17b4038b9b5891c87c998ad6e022bb5` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `11e6e9dc38c0b0ed566d8c95f236f4d686ed4c8c` — the merge of head `576a37667fd6c6430c8c1b70373214e54a71e7bb` into base `b4c99b8dd17b4038b9b5891c87c998ad6e022bb5`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 11e6e9dc38c0b0ed566d8c95f236f4d686ed4c8c && git checkout 11e6e9dc38c0b0ed566d8c95f236f4d686ed4c8c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b4c99b8dd17b4038b9b5891c87c998ad6e022bb5 576a37667fd6c6430c8c1b70373214e54a71e7bb && git checkout -B drift-repro b4c99b8dd17b4038b9b5891c87c998ad6e022bb5 && git merge --no-ff 576a37667fd6c6430c8c1b70373214e54a71e7bb

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b4c99b8dd17b4038b9b5891c87c998ad6e022bb5
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b4c99b8dd17b4038b9b5891c87c998ad6e022bb5` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

repo:objectstack#1 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4czzx9dtSEm3jWWL9c3

**L1 verdict (L1-a): ACCEPT** at head `576a37667fd6c6430c8c1b70373214e54a71e7bb` (Fixes #37953). Full read.

## Review summary

**Shape and gates.**
- `l1-face --pr 38051`: CLEAN, 13 items, none flagged.
- Check-runs at 576a37667f: 37 success, 16 expected skip, 0 failed, 0 pending.
- 4 files, +308/-32, all in `knowledge-turso` plus one changeset. Not governed, and no `packages/spec/src/**` path.

**Declarations.** `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are right, on the same reasoning this lane accepted for the pgvector fix #37942.
- The refused call is a build writing into a source `dropSource` already removed. The spec contract (`IKnowledgeAdapter.dropSource` removes every generation, the one under construction included) already forbids that write, so refusing it narrows nothing an author or caller could rely on.
- A replaced build was refused before too. The only change there is the code: `LOCK_CONFLICT` 409 instead of `KNOWLEDGE_REBUILD_REQUIRED`, or an uncoded error at completion. It now matches pgvector.
- `patch` is right, and no contract review is owed: no schema path, no governed rule text, no narrowing and no `Clause-②: yes`.

**Code read against the claim.**
- `beginBuild` records the generation it took, as number, `created_at` and fingerprint, read back after the insert. `writeTarget`, the listing and `completeBuild` accept only that generation for a `reindex` call. Anything else ends the build with `LOCK_CONFLICT` and opens nothing.
- The number alone is not enough, because the next generation is the highest plus one. The reuse case is pinned (the `reused_same` / `reused_other` cells).
- `writePassages`' in-transaction re-read now matches `created_at` too. So a page embedded across the drop's commit is written nowhere.
- A `beginBuild` that throws clears the mark. `completeBuild` clears it in `finally`.
- A build begun after the drop is unchanged.
- The README and changeset sentences match the code.

**Evidence.**
- 231/231 tests under the lock, including 30 new cells (15 × `:memory:`/`file:`).
- Two named ablations go red on the right cells: 24 cells for the write-target branch, and the 6 completion cells for the completion check.
- Dogfood is green in CI.

**Nits, optional:**
- N1: `created_at` has millisecond resolution (`strftime %f`). A drop followed by a new generation with the same number, same fingerprint and same millisecond would pass as the old one. That is not reachable in practice, since it takes two separate transactions.
- N2: the build mark is one per source per adapter. Two builds of one source in the same process share it, and the first one to complete clears it, so the second build's remaining writes go unfenced, as they all did before.
- N3: the PR body's Verification section still says NOT MEASURED; the dev report 7229379444 carries the locked runs. A body edit does not move the head.
- The two boundaries left in Acceptance notes are accepted as stated: event-sync writes after a drop open a generation, as on pgvector, and a failed walk's mark stays until the next `beginBuild`.

**Next:** not Tier H and not governed, so the area lands it.
